target.title: fix(cron): respect deliveryBestEffort in interim-message suppression guard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `deliveryBestEffort: true` is configured on a cron job, the interim-message suppression guard can still suppress delivery if `hadDescendants` is truthy (e.g. stale subagent registry entries) and the agent's reply text matches interim cron hint phrases like "on it" or "pulling everything together". The other two guards in the same function already respect `deliveryBestEffort` — this makes the third one consistent.

- Problem: `finalizeTextDelivery()` suppresses delivery for best-effort cron jobs when the reply matches interim hints and descendant state is present, even though "best effort" means delivering whatever the agent produced.
- Solution: Add the missing `!params.deliveryBestEffort &&` guard to the interim-message suppression condition at line 1498, matching the existing guards at lines 1455 and 1485.
- What changed: `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts` (+1 line condition), `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts` (updated test assertion).
- What did NOT change: Function signature, exported API, other delivery paths, outer cron scheduler, subagent followup logic.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #111359
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The `finalizeTextDelivery` function has three guards that can suppress delivery:
1. **L1455** — `!params.deliveryBestEffort && (activeSubagentRuns > 0 || expectedSubagentFollowup)` — skips waiting for subagents
2. **L1485** — `!params.deliveryBestEffort && activeSubagentRuns > 0` — skips active-subagent suppression
3. **L1498** — `hadDescendants && synthesizedText.trim() === initialSynthesizedText && isLikelyInterimCronMessage(...)` — **no `!deliveryBestEffort` guard**

Guard #3 is inconsistent with #1 and #2. When `deliveryBestEffort: true` and `hadDescendants` is truthy (e.g. from stale subagent registry entries or a completed descendant fallback), best-effort jobs that produce interim-message text have their delivery silently suppressed.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: `deliveryBestEffort: true` cron jobs no longer have delivery suppressed by the interim-message guard when `hadDescendants` is truthy
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.22.3, `fix/cron-delivery-besteffort-interim-suppress-111359`, DeepSeek V4 Pro
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
# Start gateway with fix code
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=... node dist/index.js gateway start

# Create cron job with deliveryBestEffort + spawn subagent + interim text
openclaw cron add --name "e2e-prove-delivery" \
  --at "+3m" \
  --message "Use sessions_spawn to spawn a quick subagent ... then reply 'working on it, let me compile the results'" \
  --session "isolated" \
  --best-effort-deliver \
  --channel "telegram" --to "000000"

# Run it
openclaw cron run <id>

# Check result
openclaw cron runs --id <id>
```

- Real cron execution output:

```console
$ openclaw cron runs --id 5fd661ac-8515-4a51-8924-c84167bed30f
{
  "entries": [{
    "status": "ok",
    "summary": "working on it, let me compile the results",
    "model": "deepseek-v4-pro",
    "delivered": false,
    "deliveryError": "telegram outbound adapter is unavailable.",
    "delivery": {
      "intended": { "channel": "telegram", "to": "000000", "source": "explicit" },
      "resolved": { "ok": true, "channel": "telegram", "to": "000000", "source": "explicit" },
      "fallbackUsed": true,
      "delivered": false
    }
  }]
}
```

- Unit test suite:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts --run
 RUN  v4.1.10
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  93 passed (93)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/ --run
 Test Files  34 passed (34)
      Tests  472 passed (472)
```

**Key evidence from E2E test:**

The delivery pipeline returned `deliveryError: "telegram outbound adapter is unavailable"` — this means the code reached **real outbound delivery** past the interim suppression guard. If the old (buggy) code had suppressed delivery, the result would have returned `deliveryAttempted: true` without any `deliveryError` (see lines 1508-1515). The delivery adapter was not configured (expected), but the critical point is that the fix prevented the interim suppression from blocking delivery.

**Matrix-style evidence**:

| Scenario | `deliveryBestEffort` | `activeSubagentRuns` | `hadDescendants` | Text matches interim | Delivered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Best-effort, stale descendants | `true` | 2 | `true` | `true` | ✅ Passed interim guard |
| Best-effort, no descendants | `true` | 0 | `false` | `true` | ✅ `true` (existing path) |
| Normal (not best-effort), stale descendants | `false` | 2 | `true` | `true` | ❌ `false` (suppressed — correct) |
| Normal, clean | `false` | 0 | `false` | `false` | ✅ `true` (existing path) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `deliveryBestEffort: true` + descendants + interim text → delivery proceeds (previously suppressed) ✅ **E2E confirmed**
  2. `deliveryBestEffort: true` + no descendants + interim text → delivery proceeds (unchanged)
  3. `deliveryBestEffort: false` + descendants + interim text → suppressed (unchanged — correct)
- What was not tested: Telegram delivery adapter (not configured)
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: Not needed — delivery policy has no auth implications
  - ✅ Enum completeness: Covers `deliveryBestEffort: true/false`, with/without descendants, with/without interim text
  - ✅ Path coverage: Shared `finalizeTextDelivery` covers all cron text-delivery paths
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: No new state or resources to clean up

## Root Cause

`finalizeTextDelivery()` in `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts` has three guards that can suppress or redirect delivery. Guards at lines 1455 and 1485 check `!params.deliveryBestEffort` before acting, but the interim-message suppression guard at line 1498 does not. This means `deliveryBestEffort: true` cron jobs that produce interim-style text (e.g. "on it", "pulling everything together") while the subagent registry shows active or completed descendants have their delivery silently suppressed.

The sibling guards were added in PR #52136 (subagent awareness for isolated cron) and PR #95419 (delivery best-effort mode). The interim suppression guard was added separately without the same `deliveryBestEffort` gate.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Best-effort cron jobs that produce interim acknowledgment text (like "on it") will now have that text delivered to the target channel. Previously these runs recorded `delivered: false` without error. Non-best-effort jobs are unaffected.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: All 4 input variants in the evidence matrix; all 472 isolated-agent cron tests pass; real E2E cron execution with DeepSeek V4 Pro confirmed delivery reaches outbound stage
- Edge cases checked: `deliveryBestEffort: true` with active descendants, `deliveryBestEffort: true` without descendants, `deliveryBestEffort: false` with descendants, normal clean runs
- What you did NOT verify: Real Telegram delivery (adapter not configured on test gateway)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only changes behavior for `deliveryBestEffort: true` jobs with descendant state, where delivery was incorrectly suppressed
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the `finalizeTextDelivery` function is the correct boundary because it already has sibling guards with the same pattern for `deliveryBestEffort`
- **Refactor needed**: No — single condition addition, no architecture or API changes
- **Alternative considered**: Removing the interim suppression entirely — rejected; non-best-effort jobs should still suppress stale interim text

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Best-effort cron jobs that intentionally produce interim-like text (e.g. a status job that says "working on it") will now deliver that text instead of suppressing it.

**Mitigation**: The `deliveryBestEffort` flag is explicitly configured by the operator — best-effort mode's stated contract is "deliver whatever we have." Operators who want interim suppression can remove `deliveryBestEffort: true` from their cron config.

**Compatibility impact**: None for jobs without `deliveryBestEffort: true` configured.

---

Fixes #111359
